title: Native event history does not prove consumer intent or progress
applies_when: An asynchronous stream handoff or runner registration/completion repair infers current caller intent from past events, a regression only checks state flags without exercising normal consumption, or a reproduced internal contract gap has no demonstrated shipped caller.
lesson: Use the actual runtime and owner entry to check explicit operation sequences and observable consumer progress. In Node readable streams, pause() need not emit a new pause event when already non-flowing, and removing a readable listener can schedule an automatic resume for data consumers. A historical resume event therefore cannot represent the latest caller intent. Keep pause-only, resume-then-pause, normal flowing consumption and async iteration as distinct controls; verify buffered bytes and EOF as well as state. A repair can preserve a pause flag yet stall normal consumers. Confirm that the selected tests actually ran: scoped runners can return success when their filters exclude every selected file. For GoRaven Query, a caller registering after asynchronous launch can recreate an entry already deleted by fast completion. Register after synchronous validation/persistence succeeds but before launch; remove every caller's late registration. A controlled blocking model makes immediate registration deterministic without scheduler sleeps, then release it and wait for the real completion callback before checking cleanup. Keep synchronous history-error non-registration as a control and distinguish package initialization/configuration failure from an executed regression failure.
avoid_when: These Node transition mechanisms are not universal to other stream libraries or runtime versions. A portable helper/owner-entry probe is not POSIX IPC transfer, whole-application, performance or PR qualification. Even a real-broker regression can demonstrate an internal contract gap without establishing shipped caller impact or a useful upstream behavior change; inspect actual caller timing and backpressure before expanding or publishing a repair. Do not remove buffering guards or suppress native exit draining solely from a narrow state test. Registration-before-launch fixes ordering, not atomic concurrent-start admission or ownership-safe deletion of replacement runners; those need separate evidence and synchronization. Absence of an affected caller in a reviewed snapshot is not proof that no future caller can be affected.

evidence.note: pause() emits only on a flowing-state transition; updateReadableListening may resume when data listeners remain. This pinned native implementation explains the mechanism, not a general repair guarantee.
The official reading-mode contract distinguishes flowing data consumption, readable-event consumption and asynchronous iteration. Test the intended consumer API, not a guessed common mode.

The handoff holds reads, installs a readable listener and later uses recorded resume intent. This is a source example to inspect alongside the actual caller and native runtime; it does not qualify any proposed fix.
shouldPassWithNoTestsForCliIncludes permits success when every CLI selection is excluded. Resolve the owning lane and check executed inventory; this pinned example does not describe every runner.

Published native Node 24.16 registered-suite reproduction: caller pause and resume-then-pause both fail on pinned OpenClaw source, while ten existing handoff controls pass. The report includes the runnable tests and scope limits. A local candidate's 12 passes do not imply independent review, application impact or performance qualification.

A maintainer independently confirmed both explicit-pause failures at 82949354d73, but found no affected shipped caller. Exec output never paused before publication, awaited output's Writable backpressure held at 64 KiB, the relay paused only after delivery, and other startup pauses used native spawn. The issue was closed without a broker change, with reopening conditional on an affected caller/product flow. This is a scope-specific impact counterexample, not a denial of the internal contract gap or proof that every possible consumer is safe.

Real Go 1.25.5 Query/ADK lifecycle with existing model/repository mocks: unchanged master fails only the immediate-registration assertion; repair passes all 37 agent test/subtest results, two focused race tests and vet for agent/service. Both chat and automation late registrations are removed. No external model, full application, atomic-admission or performance claim.
